one_line: The restroom trailer and its servicing fit our work, but three of the four units are commercial-code modular offices, and we have no pricing or past performance for those; this is a lowest-price award where large modular leasing firms usually bid directly, so we should bid only if a Northwest modular office partner commits to a competitive quote and to its experience by the Nov 17 site visit.
scope: WFLHD wants to lease three office units during its office renovation at 610 E. Fifth Street, Vancouver, WA: one 24' x 60' commercial-code (IBC) double-wide modular office with 3 offices, 1 secure meeting room, and 2 conference rooms, plus two 8' x 40' finished office containers or modular units. It also wants one climate-controlled executive restroom trailer with at least 3 stations. The contractor delivers, preps the site, blocks and levels the units, installs skirting, steps, and ramps, and makes certified electrical connections. It then provides 22 months of lease, maintenance, weekly septic pumping, freshwater refills, and winterization, and finishes with teardown and site restoration. All units must be ready for occupancy by 01-MAR-2027 on a firm-fixed-price order (POP 02/01/2027–01/31/2029). Award goes to the lowest-priced quote that is technically acceptable.
fit: NAICS 532490 is on our list, and our GSA SIN 532490P matches. A GSA schedule is not required, though: Q&A #1 and #6 call this an open-market, full and open buy.

Unrestricted full and open with no set-aside, so our SBE/MBE status does not block us. If we are small under the $40.0M size standard, 52.219-4 exempts an otherwise successful small business offer from the 10% HUBZone evaluation factor.

The restroom trailer, weekly pumping, freshwater refills, winterization, account management, and demobilization match our USCG Station Lake Worth Inlet work (70Z02826FMIAM0008, $78,500, 2026) and our Denver restroom trailer contract (SC-00011558, Aug 2026–ongoing).
Our capability statement lists office and classroom trailers and restroom facilities in our fleet.
Q&A #7 allows subcontracting modular unit supply, installation, utilities, and restroom services. Q&A #2 lets a subcontractor's or major supplier's experience count toward Factor 2C.

No mandatory site visit (Q&A #8), no bonding stated, and no permits or stamped drawings required (Q&A #39, #48). The Government pays utilities and provides furniture, internet, network hardware, and recurring restroom supplies (Q&A #20, #29, #41, #42).
Q&A #43 accepts previously used units in good operating condition. This is a new contract with no incumbent (Q&A #9).
SAM is active (UEI REVFD44JLMV5, CAGE 57C31). If our past performance is too thin to rate, Factor 3 is scored neutral (Addendum para 5.a.ii; Q&A #10).
red_flags: Lowest price technically acceptable: only the lowest-priced acceptable quote wins (52.212-2 Addendum, Basis for Award). National modular firms win these directly. Williams Scotsman took $146,238 (Yuma office trailers) and $349,238 (Dugway command post trailers, 11 offers). As prime, our markup on a modular subcontractor puts us at a price disadvantage.
Partial quotes are rejected (Q&A #11), so we cannot quote only the restroom trailer.

Factor 2C is pass/fail and requires at least 5 years of relevant experience within the last 7, at similar size and scope. Our documented work since Nov 2019 is about 3–3.5 years combined (Camp Lejeune, Fort Lee, Portsmouth, USCG, Denver), and none of it is modular offices. The Navy Oregon job (2018–2019) falls outside the window. We likely need the subcontractor's experience to pass.
Our price list has no rows for modular offices or office containers, so we have no basis to price 3 of the 4 units.

Our template servicing rate does not fit this job. $5,000/week (from a 30-day USCG quote) over about 95 weeks comes to about $475,000, which is more than the $450,000 top of the estimate. Weekly service has to be priced with a local pumper.
Units must meet IBC commercial occupancy, and residential (IRC) units are prohibited (SOW 6.1.1). Our HUD/HCD approvals do not show IBC commercial compliance.

The site is about 1,000 miles from our Marina del Rey base. The 24-month firm-fixed price includes all repair labor and parts at no extra cost (SOW 5.3.1), a 4-hour emergency and 24-hour routine response (Q&A #27), and cold-weather operation.

Site facts that drive cost (panel capacity, run distances, anchoring, water tap, pump-truck reach) are only available at the Nov 17 site visit (Q&A #16, #21, #22, #38). Under FAR 52.237-1, failing to inspect is no basis for a claim after award.

Conflicts between the SOW and Q&A answers that are not yet in an amendment: preventive maintenance is quarterly for the offices (SOW 5.3) vs. monthly for all units (Q&A #37); skirting on the 8x40s (SOW 5.2.4 vs. Q&A #14); hose connection to municipal water (SOW 6.3.4) vs. 'temporary holding/water tanks will be required' (Q&A #42); hours of 7:30–5:30 (Q&A #18) vs. 7:30–4:30 (Q&A #40). Amendment 0003 deletes the Cat6 pre-wiring, but its continuation pages still print that text.
Certifying electrical connections to NEC from 125-amp panels (SOW 5.2.6) requires a qualified electrical subcontractor in Washington.
PSC W054 is not one of our listed PSCs (W023, W099, W045).
competition: There is no incumbent; this is a new contract (Q&A #9). This agency's past NAICS 532490 awards are not comparable: McClain & received $54,750 for an under-bridge inspection vehicle (2 offers, small business set-aside, 2021), and Bridge Access Specialties received $38,689 sole source (2020). Likely competitors, based on the NAICS 532490 + PSC W054 benchmarks, are national modular leasing firms. Williams Scotsman appears repeatedly ($146,238 Yuma office trailers, 4 offers; $349,238 Dugway command post trailers, 11 offers; $56,076 Providence trailer lease; $46,138 Phoenix modular building). Others are Monmouth Solutions ($131,670 Red Rock mobile office trailer, 8 offers, small business set-aside) and Pacific Mobile Structures ($137,830 Kings Bay two-story modular, 1 offer). Offer counts on office and modular leases ranged from 1 to 11. The interested-vendor list is on SAM.gov behind sign-in (Q&A #12) and is not in the bid pack.
price_signal: SAM.gov's estimated value is $150,000–$450,000. The independent government cost estimate is not disclosed. Comparable office and modular leases: Williams Scotsman $146,238 (Yuma, about 11 months) and $349,238 (Dugway, 12 months); Monmouth Solutions $131,670 (Red Rock mobile office trailer); Pacific Mobile Structures $137,830 (Kings Bay two-story modular); Valcorp $173,135 (Mountain Home AFB trailer lease, 24 months, 8(a) sole source); Nazareth $115,096 and $55,217 (portable buildings and offices, about 1 month). Our own data covers only the restroom portion. The closest price-list row is a 13ft Luxury Shower-Restroom Combination Trailer (3 stalls), listed at '2495-3995' for 'More than 3 Months', with no billing basis stated. The price list has no modular office or office container rows. Template reference: $8,995/unit restroom trailer rental and $5,000/week servicing on a 30-day USCG job. That servicing rate does not scale to 22 months. [CONFIRM: modular office subcontractor pricing; local weekly pumping cost; restroom trailer monthly rate]
must_have: Completed SF18 with blocks 8, 12, 13, 14, 15, and 16 filled in, and our UEI in block 8 (RFQ checklist; 52.212-1 Addendum item 1.a; 52.204-7(b)(1)(ii)). Signer: Kermit Pemberton, President/Director.

Completed Section B price schedule: CLIN 00101 lease (22 MO), 00201 installation (LS), 00301 monthly maintenance (22 MO), 00401 teardown (LS), plus grand total. Prices include all taxes (52.212-1 Addendum item 1.b; 52.212-4(k)). Partial months are prorated, and 52.217-8 extensions (up to 6 months) are at the same rates (Q&A #13).

Technical narrative explaining how each SOW requirement will be met, including logistics and schedule. List any technical assumptions, conditions, or exceptions; if none are listed, we are assumed to accept everything (52.212-1 Addendum, item 2.a and preamble).

Cut sheets, spec sheets, and drawings proving every unit meets the minimums (Addendum 2.b; Factor 2B): IBC commercial occupancy, no IRC (SOW 6.1.1); 24x60 with at least 2.0-ton HVAC, STC 40+ floor-to-ceiling partitions, at least 2 exterior doors, ADA (SOW 5.1.1, 6.2.1); 8x40s with at least 1.5-ton HVAC (SOW 6.2.2); restroom trailer no older than 7 years, at least 3 stations, waterless urinal, separate men's and women's exterior doors, 150-gal fresh / 560-gal waste tanks, arctic package, 120V with no more than 3–4 30A cords (SOW 5.1.3, 6.1.3, 6.3); cipher lock on the secure room (Q&A #19b).

Relevant experience within the last 7 years, max 5 pages, on Attachment 0002 or our own format at no more than 1 page per reference (Addendum 2.c). Must show at least 5 years of relevant experience at similar size and scope (Factor 2C). Subcontractor experience may be used if submitted (Q&A #2).

Past performance within the last 3 years, max 10 pages: work description, dates, client, and a contact phone and email for each (Addendum 2.d). Must cover both the prime and the subcontractor (Q&A #3). References email the PPQ (Attachment 0003) to WFL.Purchasing@dot.gov with subject 'Source Selection Information: 69056726Q000042 PPQ for RFQ 69056727Q000005' (Amendment 0001, page E-14).

Completed Section E para 1 reps and certs (52.209-2, 52.209-11, 52.219-1, 52.204-5 if applicable), plus the signed TAR 1252.237-71 Certification of Data with matching certifications from our subcontractors (Section E; Addendum 2.e).
'Reps and Certs FAR Report' from our SAM.gov account; SAM reps must have been updated within the last year (Addendum 2.f; RFQ checklist).
Acknowledgment of Amendments 0001, 0002, and 0003 (Addendum 2.g; SF30 block 11).
A statement of the extent of our agreement with all terms, conditions, and amendments (52.212-1(a)(6)). Prices held firm for 60 days (52.212-1(b)).

Submit as PDF or another fixed-layout format by email to WFL.Purchasing@dot.gov with the RFQ number in the subject line. No password protection, marketing materials, or letters of support (Addendum as amended by Amendment 0001).
Comply with Service Contract Act wage determination 2015-5563 Rev. 30 (Clark County, WA). All prescribed labor is covered by this WD (Attachment 0004; Q&A #34).

Performance terms: units turnkey ready for occupancy by 01-MAR-2027 (SOW 5.1; Q&A #31); coordinate with the TPOC at least 10 business days before delivery (SOW 3); no ground penetration, but ballast and wind-load anchoring allowed (Q&A #22, #47); 7-day notice for any outage (Q&A #22); supervisor on site during setup and takedown (Q&A #40); re-leveling 30–60 days after initial occupancy (SOW 5.2.7; Q&A #30); weekly septic pumping with a certified pumper truck (SOW 5.3.1); demobilization 01-JAN to 31-JAN-2029 (SOW 5.4; Q&A #32).
REAL ID required for site access (Amendment 0002, para 3.1; Q&A #18).
gaps: [CONFIRM: modular office partner] Who supplies and services the IBC commercial 24' x 60' double-wide and the two 8' x 40' office units in the Pacific Northwest? We need their firm price, availability by 01-MAR-2027, cut sheets, 5+ years of relevant experience, and past performance from the last 3 years. Also confirm they will team with us and not quote WFLHD directly.
[CONFIRM: our office trailer fleet] The capability statement lists office trailers, but no unit count, sizes, code compliance (IBC vs. HUD/HCD), or location is documented.

[CONFIRM: restroom trailer] Do we have a restroom-only unit (our priced 3-stall unit is a shower-restroom combo) that is no older than 7 years, with 3+ stations, a waterless urinal, separate men's and women's exterior doors, 150/560-gal tanks, an arctic package, and 120V/30A cords? Where is it located?
[CONFIRM: size status] Are we small under NAICS 532490 ($40.0M) in SAM? This decides the 52.219-4 10% evaluation factor.

[CONFIRM: site visit attendee] Who attends the Nov 17, 10:00 am PST site visit (REAL ID required), and what is the travel cost? RSVP with company name, attendee names, and contact information to WFL.Purchasing@dot.gov.

[CONFIRM: local subcontractors] We need a Washington electrical subcontractor to certify NEC panel connections, plus a Vancouver-area certified pumper for weekly septic and greywater service, freshwater tank refills, and the 4-hour emergency response.
[CONFIRM: monthly servicing cost] What do local pumping and preventive maintenance cost per month? Our $5,000/week template rate would exceed the estimate.

[CONFIRM: binding scope] Will the Q&A answers be incorporated by amendment? Specifically: preventive maintenance quarterly vs. monthly (Q&A #37); skirting on the 24x60 only (Q&A #14); ramps on the 24x60 and restroom trailer only (Q&A #15); Cat6 pre-wiring removed (Amendment 0003; Q&A #46); temporary water tanks vs. hose to municipal water (Q&A #42 vs. SOW 6.3.4); operating hours 5:30 vs. 4:30 pm. If not, submit questions by 01-DEC-2026, 4:00 pm PT.

[CONFIRM: experience math] Can we document 5 years of relevant experience in the last 7 ourselves? Our in-window record totals about 3–3.5 years. Portsmouth (ended Nov 2023) may fall outside the 3-year past performance window by Dec 8, 2026.

[CONFIRM: past performance data] The Denver contract value is printed as '~$100,00.00'. The ECC Camp Lejeune term is listed as '1 year' but the dates show May 2020–Oct 2021. We need reference contacts willing to return the PPQ.
[CONFIRM: proposal email] Which email do we use on proposals: sales@temporarykitchens123.com or contract@temporary123.com?

[CONFIRM: insurance and warranty] What insurance coverage do we carry for full commercial warranty, repair, and damage risk over a 24-month firm-fixed-price lease? The solicitation states no insurance or bonding requirement.
deadline: Quotes are due Tuesday, 08-DEC-2026, 2:00 pm PT, by email to WFL.Purchasing@dot.gov (Amendment 0002 replaced 24-NOV-2026; Amendment 0003 did not change it). Technical questions are due Tuesday, 01-DEC-2026, 4:00 pm PT. The organized site visit (not mandatory, RSVP required) is Tuesday, 17-NOV-2026, 10:00 am PST at the WFLHD Main Entrance, 610 E 5th Street, Vancouver, WA. Anticipated award is 12/15/2026.
